_comment: Each source carries: id, name, url, tier, verified, newest_seen. Tier 1 = primary institutional source (legislation, official press, court output). Tier 2 = supporting, national or journalistic. 'verified' means the endpoint was fetched by hand and returned a parseable feed. 'newest_seen' is the date of the newest item it held at that moment - because a feed can parse perfectly and still be dead. 'score_multiplier' down-weights sources that are useful but not authoritative. Never mark a source verified you have not actually fetched.
_audit: 2026-08-31 - portfolio rebuilt, then corrected against a real collection run (Actions run #8) rather than hand fetches. 20 entries, 16 enabled and all 16 returning a healthy feed, newest item 0-6 days old. 4 entries deliberately disabled and documented: the three European Parliament feeds return an empty response to GitHub's runners, and Euractiv returns 403 to them - both are access blocks at the far end, not faults here. FIXED: ec-presscorner was returning month-old items because the 'pagesize' parameter breaks the API's newest-first ordering. REMOVED: european-council (meetings.ashx now 404s), council-acts (raw register, low editorial value next to council-eu), ep-think-tank (never verified). ADDED: commons-library, ukandeu, cer, euronews-europe. NOTE: hand-fetching a feed and letting the runner fetch it give different answers - council-eu and the EUR-Lex feeds looked stale by hand and are current from Actions. Trust the run's source-health table over any manual check. Verified alternates not included: bruegel.org/rss.xml, instituteforgovernment.org.uk/rss.xml.

sources.name: European Commission - press corner
sources.note: Live, same-day. Do NOT add a pagesize parameter: it silently breaks the newest-first ordering and the feed starts returning month-old items while still parsing perfectly. That is what made this look dead through August.

sources.name: European Parliament - press releases
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. europarl.europa.eu returns an empty response (0 bytes) to GitHub's runners - not a parsing problem, an access one. Kept in the file, switched off, so the Parliament gap stays visible instead of failing every run. Re-enable and run a health check if you ever move collection off GitHub Actions.

sources.name: European Parliament - committee press releases
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. Same block as ep-press: empty response from GitHub's runners. Editorially this is the feed worth fighting for - committee stage is where a law's wording actually changes - so re-test it first if collection ever moves off Actions.

sources.name: European Parliament - texts adopted
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. Same block as ep-press. EUR-Lex partly covers the same ground: adopted texts reach the Official Journal feed eventually.

sources.name: Council of the EU - press releases
sources.note: Live and current: run #8 saw 20 items, newest 2 days old. It carries its timestamp in an Atom-namespaced <a10:updated> tag rather than <pubDate>, which collect.py has handled since the 26 Aug parser fix.

sources.name: EUR-Lex - Commission proposals
sources.note: The healthiest EUR-Lex feed and the one that matters most: proposals are where a law starts. Titles are CELEX identifiers with truncated descriptions, so keyword scoring on the title under-performs - hence the multiplier. Slow to respond, hence the raised timeout.

sources.name: EUR-Lex - case law
sources.note: The only route to Court of Justice output in this set - the Court's own site publishes no usable RSS (checked 31 Aug 2026). Roughly a third of its items carry no readable item-level date, so date_fallback is set to 'channel'.

sources.name: EUR-Lex - Official Journal L (acts in force)
sources.note: Law as published. Batch feed, so it arrives in lumps rather than steadily. Same CELEX title problem as the proposals feed.

sources.name: European Central Bank - press
sources.note: Live and current. Rates, supervision and the digital euro - the money-and-work beat leans on this.

sources.name: gov.uk - news and communications
sources.note: Live, very high volume, all of Whitehall. The workhorse of the UK side. The noise list in rules.json does the real filtering; add a keywords parameter to narrow at source if it ever overwhelms a run.

sources.name: House of Commons Library - research briefings
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. Impartial explanatory briefings written for non-specialists, which is the closest thing in the set to what Passerelle itself is trying to be. Frequently covers UK-EU divergence directly.

sources.name: UK Parliament - all bills
sources.note: Live. Dates live in <a10:updated>, not <pubDate>. High volume on a first run - expect the whole live bill list at once, then only movements.

sources.name: gov.uk - Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
sources.note: Live, but roughly nine in ten items are travel advice and consular guidance. The noise list kills those; without it this feed alone would dominate the digest.

sources.name: gov.uk - Department for Business and Trade
sources.note: The best divergence source in the set - UKCA/CE marking, trade remedies, market access. Consider promoting to tier 1.

sources.name: UK in a Changing Europe
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. ESRC-funded academic initiative writing about nothing except the UK-EU relationship, non-partisan and readable. The closest fit to this project's subject of any source here.

sources.name: Centre for European Reform
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. Pro-European reformist think tank, London and Brussels. Useful for the argument behind a development rather than the fact of it - treat as context, not as a primary claim.

sources.name: EUobserver
sources.note: Verified 31 Aug 2026. Independent Brussels newsroom, strong on institutional accountability. Journalism, not a primary source - always follow it back to the document.

sources.name: Politico Europe
sources.note: Fast and well sourced on Brussels process. Same rule as EUobserver: it tells you something is happening, the document tells you what.

sources.name: Euractiv
sources.note: DISABLED 31 Aug 2026. Returns HTTP 403 to GitHub's runners, though it serves a browser fine - the runner IP range is blocked. Nothing to fix at this end.

sources.name: Euronews - My Europe
sources.note: Added 31 Aug 2026. The European-politics vertical specifically, not the general news feed. Broadest and most general of the media sources, hence the lowest multiplier - useful mainly for spotting what has broken through to a mainstream audience.
